"\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE) list_of_df = lapply(1:length(vct_files), function(ifile){ read_parquet(vct_files[ifile]) }) vct <- bind_rows(list_of_df) invisible(gc()) ## Do the actual gridding now vct["fsc_small_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["fsc_small"]], grid_bins[["fsc_small"]], labels = FALSE, right = FALSE)) vct["pe_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["pe"]], grid_bins[["pe"]], labels = FALSE, right = FALSE)) vct["chl_small_coord"] <- as.integer(cut(vct[["chl_small"]], grid_bins[["chl_small"]], labels = FALSE, right = FALSE)) ## Remove beads vct = vct %>% filter(pop != "beads") ## Gridding the data and summing the Qcs in each 3d grid bin. gridded <- vct %>% group_by(date, across(ends_with("_coord")), pop) %>% summarise(Qc = sum(Qc), .groups="drop") %>% select(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord, Qc) %>% arrange(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord) ## Aggregate to hourly level hourly_gridded <- gridded %>% group_by(date=floor_date(date, "1 hours"), across(ends_with("_coord"))) %>% summarise(Qc=sum(Qc), .groups="drop") %>% arrange(date, fsc_small_coord, chl_small_coord, pe_coord) invisible(gc()) ## Each cruise's binned data is now saved to a file 4 Ocean Environmental Covariates for Seaflow cruises 4.1 Loading and visualizing data knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE) library(tidyverse) library(cmap4r) library(cruisedat) ## Output directory here::i_am("01-process-seaflow.Rmd") ## setwd("~/repos/process-data") ## here() starts at /Users/sangwonh/repos/process-data outputdir = "output/seaflow-covariates" ##outputdir = "~/Dropbox/data/ocean/seaflow/2025-09-15" dir.create(outputdir, showWarnings = FALSE) ## Helpers ## source("02-helpers.R") ## Other setup ## colocalized_csvfile = file.path(outputdir, paste0(cruisename, "-from-CMAP.csv")) We’ll procure the environmental covariates that go along with seaflow cruises, from Simons CMAP. What are all the tables and variables we need? ## Get authorization cmap4r::set_authorization(reset = FALSE, cmap_key = "ec7b8400-e5ae-11eb-88c6-c79daf4f0e4a") ## Get the cadtalog catalog = cmap4r::get_catalog() ## Do colocalization ## cmap4r::get_cruises() targetVars = catalog %>% filter(Table_Name == "tblPisces_NRT") %>% pull(Variable) dat = cmap4r::along_track("MGL1704", targetTables = "tblPisces_NRT", targetVars = "Fe", temporalTolerance = 3.5, latTolerance = 5, lonTolerance = 5, depthTolerance = 10, depth1 = 0, depth2 = 10) dat %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=time, y= Fe)) ## This will further be averaged into unique hours. dat %>% mutate(hourly_time = lubridate::floor_date(time, unit = "hours")) %>% group_by(hourly_time) %>% summarize(Fe = mean(Fe, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=hourly_time, y= Fe)) ## Then, the coverage is assessed. dat %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(y=lat, x=lon, col = Fe)) ## repodir = "~/repos/cruisedat" ## outputdir = "." ## dir.create(file.path(".", "export"), showWarnings = FALSE) (It may not be practical to simply pull all data from all tables, as I used to back in 2019.) I realize there are at least three types of covariates. Collected directly on the ship. Each cruise’s webpage shows a list of these. One probably needs to go over these manually, and selectively download them. Also, there are measurements that are taken sparsely along a cruise track, sometimes at depth. These are only useful if they can be reasonably interpolated from the original resolution to the hourly level. In situ drifter/float Global Drifter Program: (1979-02-15 – 2019-08-07): tblGlobalDrifterProgram Argo Float Core Profiles (1997-07-28 – 2024-06-09): tblArgoCore_REP_Jun2024 I’m guessing this is the latest updated version. Others include: tblArgoCore_REP_Feb2024, tblArgoCore_REP_Nov2023, tblArgoCore_REP Argo Float Biogeochemical Profiles (2002-09-08 – 2024-06-08) tblArgoBGC_REP_Jun2024 I’m guessing this is the latest updated version. Others include: tblArgoBGC_REP, tblArgoBGC_REP_Feb2024, tblArgoBGC_REP_Nov2023, tblArgoBGC_REP_Jun2023 GEOTRACES Intermediate Data Product 2021 v2 - Seawater (2006-07-13 – 2018-11-22): tblGeotraces_Seawater_IDP2021v2 UCSD Argo Mixed Layer Depth Climatology Model 2022: tblArgo_MLD_2022_Climatology Seems super relevant Also similar to tblArgo_MLD_Climatology Models (climatology) Mercator-Pisces Biogeochemistry and Weekly Forecast (2011-12-31 to 2019-04-27): tblPisces_NRT GOBAI-O2 Climatology v2.2 (Gridded Ocean Biogeochemistry from Artificial Intelligence - Oxygen) Mercator-Pisces Biogeochemistry Daily Forecast Nutrients (2022-01-01 to 2025-07-18): tblPisces_Forecast_Nutrients Darwin Biogeochemistry 3 Day Averaged Model (1994-01-03 to 2015-12-30): tblDarwin_Nutrient World Ocean Atlas 2013 v2 Climatology: tblWOA_Climatology MODIS Chlorophyll Concentration (2002-07-04 to 2022-06-10): tblModis_CHL MODIS Photosynthetically Available Radiation Daily 9km (2010-01-01 to 2022-03-07): tblModis_PAR Other less promising models Mercator-Pisces Biogeochemistry Daily Forecast Car: (2022-01-01 – 2025-07-18): tblPisces_Forecast_Car Mercator-Pisces Biogeochemistry Daily Forecast Pft: (2022-01-01 – 2025-07-18): tblPisces_Forecast_Pft GOBAI-O2 Climatology v2.2 Gridded Ocean Biogeochemistry from Artificial Intelligence - Oxygen (UNknown time range): tblGOBAI_O2_v2_2_Climatology Mercator-Pisces Biogeochemistry Daily Forecast Co2 (2022-01-01 to 2025-07-18): tblPisces_Forecast_Co2 So, a strategy is to go through these steps: - Manually co-localize the above tables and all sensible variables therein. - Examine the on-cruise measurements (from, e.g., https://simonscmap.com/catalog/cruises/MGL1704 for Gradients 2), by 1. Excluding any gated products (which will have lots of observations, thousands or tens of thousands), 2. Exclude any things that are related to other non-Seaflow cytometers (IFCB, or imaging flow cytobot, which measures large particles above 3microns, which is larger than the small picophytoplankton we want to study), 3. Exclude any datasets that have too few surface observations (fewer than 30 rows altogether, or in the “DEPTH” visualization tab, fewer than 30-ish observations on the surface.) 4. Exclude GRUMP altogether. Next, for every model/climatology or drift/floater dataset, we need to use a for-loop that goes over a time radius of {1 hr, 1 day, 3.5 days, 14 days}, and a latitude+longitude box of side lengths {0.1 degrees, 1 degrees, 2 degrees, 5 degrees}. (I have some code lying around (in github repository sangwon-hyun/many-cruises) that can do this.)
